added_lemmas.statement:
Response-boundary failure under bounded-Lipschitz approximation.  For the singleton class \(\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\) in \(\mathrm{def:response\text{-}boundary\text{-}singleton}\), one has \(\mathbb P^0\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\), and the two bounded-Lipschitz approximation conditions hold with their suprema restricted to \(\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\):
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}}
\sup_{\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{BL}}\leq1}
\left|
E_{\mathbb P}f\!\left(\sqrt n(\widehat\beta_n-\beta_n)\right)
-E f(G_{\mathbb P,n})
\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}}
\Pr_{\mathbb P}\!\left\{
\sup_{\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{BL}}\leq1}
\left|E_{\mathbb P}^{\star}f(G_n^\star)-E f(G_{\mathbb P,n})\right|>\epsilon
\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Nevertheless, the same fixed experiment \(\mathbb P^0\), chosen independently of the numerical schedule, satisfies
\[
\exists\mathbb P^0\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\quad
\forall t=(t_n)_{n\geq1}\ \text{with }t_n>0\text{ and }t_n\to0,qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left\{
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right\}
\leq1-e^{-\lambda}<1-\alpha.
\]
Thus uniform bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximation, even over a singleton class that can be embedded in the proposed sufficient margin-rate regime, does not by itself supply the response anti-concentration or relative variance control needed for coverage when the response variance collapses.  This is a response-boundary failure, not a sharp rare-margin threshold, and its conclusion has no condition on \(n\kappa_n^3\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def:response\text{-}boundary\text{-}singleton}\), the two deployment margins of \(\mathbb P^0\) equal \(1/2\), every response-study cell probability equals \(1/4\), and \(\kappa_n\leq1/4\).  Hence
\[
\min_c p_{n,c}\wedge\min_x r_{n,x}=\frac12\geq\kappa_n,
\qquad
\min_{c,x}\pi_{n,cx}=\frac14\geq\kappa_n.
\tag{1}
\]
The response means satisfy \(0<\lambda/n<1\), because \(0<\lambda<1\).  Thus (1), the fixed finite supports, and the independent row sampling specified in \(\mathrm{def:response\text{-}boundary\text{-}singleton}\) verify every membership condition in \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}experiment}\), so
\[
\mathbb P^0\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}.
\tag{2}
\]

Let
\[
D_n(\mathbb P)=
\sup_{\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{BL}}\leq1}
\left|
E_{\mathbb P}f\!\left(\sqrt n(\widehat\beta_n-\beta_n)\right)
-E f(G_{\mathbb P,n})
\right|
\]
and
\[
M_n(\mathbb P)=
\sup_{\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{BL}}\leq1}
\left|E_{\mathbb P}^{\star}f(G_n^\star)-E f(G_{\mathbb P,n})\right|.
\]
Since \(\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}=\{\mathbb P^0\}\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}}D_n(\mathbb P)=D_n(\mathbb P^0),
\qquad
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}}
\Pr_{\mathbb P}\{M_n(\mathbb P)>\epsilon\}
=\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\{M_n(\mathbb P^0)>\epsilon\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The data law, ridge estimator, and multiplier in \(\mathrm{def:response\text{-}boundary\text{-}singleton}\) are exactly those of \(\mathrm{lem:vanishing\text{-}variance\text{-}all\text{-}zero\text{-}certificate}\).  That lemma proves
\[
D_n(\mathbb P^0)\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
M_n(\mathbb P^0)=o_{\mathbb P^0}(1).
\tag{4}
\]
For every \(\epsilon>0\), the second relation in (4) gives
\(\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\{M_n(\mathbb P^0)>\epsilon\}\to0\).  Substitution into (3) proves both displayed uniform approximation assertions.  Notice that the only uniformization step is equality (3); no rate for \(\kappa_n\) is used.

Now define the all-zero response event
\[
A_n=\{Y_1=\cdots=Y_n=0\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:vanishing\text{-}variance\text{-}all\text{-}zero\text{-}certificate}\),
\[
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}(A_n)=\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^n
\longrightarrow e^{-\lambda}.
\tag{5}
\]
The same lemma proves, simultaneously for every deterministic schedule with \(t_n>0\), that on \(A_n\)
\[
L(\beta_n)=U(\beta_n)=\frac{\lambda}{n},
\qquad
F(\widehat\beta_n)=\left(\frac an,\frac an\right),
\qquad
q_{1-\alpha,n}^{\star}=0.
\tag{6}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}confidence\text{-}envelope}\), (6) implies
\[
\mathrm{CI}_n(t)=\left[\frac an,\frac an\right]
\quad\text{on }A_n.
\tag{7}
\]
Because \(0<a<\lambda\), equations (6)--(7) show
\[
A_n\subseteq
\left\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\not\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}
\quad\text{for every }t.
\tag{8}
\]
The law \(\mathbb P^0\) in (8) does not depend on \(t\).  Therefore, for every admissible deterministic schedule,
\[
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left\{
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right\}
\leq1-\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}(A_n).
\tag{9}
\]
Taking upper limits in (9) and using (5) yields
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left\{
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right\}
\leq1-e^{-\lambda}.
\tag{10}
\]
The choice \(\lambda< -\log\alpha\) gives \(e^{-\lambda}>\alpha\), hence
\[
1-e^{-\lambda}<1-\alpha.
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (10)--(11) establish the stated schedule-independent failure with the required quantifier order.

For completeness, this response-boundary failure can occur inside the proposed sufficient margin-rate regime without making that rate part of the theorem.  Choose
\[
\kappa_n=\frac{1}{4n^{1/4}}.
\]
Then (1) still holds and
\[
n\kappa_n^3=\frac{n^{1/4}}{64}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{12}
\]
The schedule \(t_n=n^{-5/16}\) also satisfies
\[
(n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=2n^{-3/8}=o(n^{-5/16}),
\qquad
n^{-5/16}=o(\kappa_n).
\tag{13}
\]
Since (10) holds for every schedule, it holds in particular for the schedule in (13).  Thus the obstruction is collapsing response variance and the resulting failure of coverage at a degenerate limit, rather than failure of the proposed margin-rate inequalities.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
The response-boundary theorem shows that \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}primitive\text{-}clt}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}multiplier\text{-}law}\) alone do not imply coverage, even over a singleton experiment class satisfying the proposed margin-rate window.  First determine a minimal, faithfully stated, independently checkable uniform response condition that excludes the collapsing-variance construction without assuming the desired critical-value or coverage conclusion.  Candidate ingredients include response-interiority, nondegeneracy of endpoint-relevant variances, relative consistency of the multiplier variance, or quantitative anti-concentration.  Then, over the subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) satisfying the selected condition, determine whether
\[
n\kappa_n^3\to\infty,
\qquad
(n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n),
\qquad
t_n=o(\kappa_n)
\]
imply
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P}
\Pr_{\mathbb P}\!\left\{
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right\}\geq1-\alpha,
\]
where the infimum is over that repaired subclass.  The additional condition must be stated in primitive response-law or multiplier-law terms and must not encode coverage itself.  This question concerns sufficiency only; whether \(n\kappa_n^3\) is sharp for rare-margin optimal-face switching remains a separate question after the response-boundary prerequisite is settled.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current question asks for coverage from two bounded-Lipschitz approximations and rate conditions alone, but the proved singleton response-boundary construction satisfies those approximations and can satisfy the rate window while its coverage stays strictly below the nominal level. The revised question first requires a noncircular response regularity condition and then asks the original sufficiency question only on the resulting subclass.

proposed.name: singleton response-boundary experiment class
proposed.construction:
Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), choose constants \(0<a<\lambda<\min\{1,-\log\alpha\}\), and let \(\kappa_n\downarrow0\) satisfy \(\kappa_n\leq 1/4\) for every \(n\).  On \(\mathcal C=\mathcal X=\{1,2\}\), define \(\mathbb P^0=(P_n^{\circ,0})_{n\geq1}\) as follows.  Row \(n\) contains \(n\) independent response-study observations \((W_i,Y_i)\), where \(W_i\) is uniform on \(\mathcal C\times\mathcal X\) and
\[
Y_i\mid W_i=(c,x)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\lambda/n).
\]
The deployment margins are observed without error and satisfy \(p_n=r_n=(1/2,1/2)\), while \(\pi_{n,cx}=1/4\) and \(\mu_{n,cx}=\lambda/n\) for every \((c,x)\).  If \(\overline Y_{n,cx}\) is the within-cell response proportion, set it to zero when the cell is empty and use
\[
\widehat\mu_{n,cx}=\left(1-\frac{2a}{n}\right)\overline Y_{n,cx}+\frac{a}{n}.
\]
The multiplier draw is the empirical-influence multiplier for these four response estimators and has zero margin coordinates.  Define the singleton experiment class
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}=\{\mathbb P^0\}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive requires the all-zero construction to generate an explicit singleton experiment class over which both uniform approximation suprema become verified single-array discrepancies.

proposed.statement:
The response-boundary theorem shows that \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}primitive\text{-}clt}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:uniform\text{-}multiplier\text{-}law}\) alone do not imply coverage, even over a singleton experiment class satisfying the proposed margin-rate window.  First determine a minimal, faithfully stated, independently checkable uniform response condition that excludes the collapsing-variance construction without assuming the desired critical-value or coverage conclusion.  Candidate ingredients include response-interiority, nondegeneracy of endpoint-relevant variances, relative consistency of the multiplier variance, or quantitative anti-concentration.  Then, over the subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) satisfying the selected condition, determine whether
\[
n\kappa_n^3\to\infty,
\qquad
(n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n),
\qquad
t_n=o(\kappa_n)
\]
imply
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P}
\Pr_{\mathbb P}\!\left\{
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right\}\geq1-\alpha,
\]
where the infimum is over that repaired subclass.  The additional condition must be stated in primitive response-law or multiplier-law terms and must not encode coverage itself.  This question concerns sufficiency only; whether \(n\kappa_n^3\) is sharp for rare-margin optimal-face switching remains a separate question after the response-boundary prerequisite is settled.
proposed.justification: The sufficiency frontier is meaningful only after the response-boundary obstruction is excluded by a primitive, noncircular regularity condition.
proposed.gap: The proved singleton theorem shows that uniform bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximation do not imply coverage at collapsing response variance. The missing step is to formulate a minimal faithful response-interiority, variance, relative-consistency, or anti-concentration condition and then prove uniform face and quantile stability under the proposed rate window.
proposed.consumer: A positive answer on a transparently repaired class would give practitioners a checkable tuning regime while identifying the response support or variance conditions required before rare-margin rates are relevant.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The revised claim depends on the new response-boundary theorem and removes the false implication from the unrepaired experiment class.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Identify a minimal noncircular uniform response-law or resampling condition that excludes response-boundary degeneration, then determine whether the proposed margin and numerical-step rates imply simultaneous endpoint coverage on that repaired class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximations are absolute metrics and remain valid when all endpoint-relevant variances collapse. They therefore provide neither relative variance consistency nor anti-concentration at the critical quantile, and the singleton construction gives actual undercoverage under every deterministic schedule.
open_obligations.attempted: The direct route from uniform bounded-Lipschitz approximation through the joint directional derivative and numerical delta map was stress-tested on the vanishing Bernoulli response array. Both approximation errors vanish, but the all-zero event has a nonvanishing probability and forces a zero multiplier critical value, so the route fails before rare-margin face localization becomes relevant.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved response-boundary theorem constructs one fixed \(2\times2\) experiment \(\mathbb P^0\) such that both bounded-Lipschitz approximation discrepancies converge to zero, but for every deterministic schedule \(t\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left\{[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\}
\leq1-e^{-\lambda}<1-\alpha.
\]
The remaining problem is therefore not derivable from the frozen approximation assumptions: it first requires a noncircular uniform response-interiority, nondegenerate-variance, relative variance-consistency, or anti-concentration condition, followed by a new uniform face-localization and quantile argument under the displayed \(\kappa_n\) and \(t_n\) rates.

prose_updates.tldr: The selector envelope and its fixed-law directional inference remain established supporting results, but the proposed rare-margin rate window is not sufficient on the unrepaired triangular-array class. A new schedule-independent response-boundary theorem constructs a singleton experiment class on which both uniform bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximations hold while simultaneous coverage is at most \(1-e^{-\lambda}<1-\alpha\). The uniform frontier must therefore begin by imposing a faithful response-interiority, nondegenerate-variance, relative variance-consistency, or anti-concentration condition; only then is the sufficiency or sharpness of \(n\kappa_n^3\) a meaningful open question.

project_justification.gap: Cho--Russell and Gafarov provide uniform LP inference under different perturbation, regularization, and fixed-regularity frameworks. For the row-feasible paired numerical-delta procedure, the present theorem additionally shows that absolute bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximation is inadequate when response variance collapses. Existing comparisons therefore do not supply either the missing response regularity condition or the rare-margin face-switching analysis on the repaired class.
project_justification.niche: The remaining field-level niche has two ordered parts: first characterize a primitive and noncircular response regularity condition sufficient for uniform critical-value behavior; then determine the procedure-specific shrinking-margin boundary and tuning window under that condition. The proved singleton theorem is a negative prerequisite result, not a sharp rare-margin threshold.
project_justification.fill: The project gives an explicit all-zero response construction and the singleton class \(\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\), proves that both bounded-Lipschitz approximation suprema reduce to discrepancies that vanish on this class, and nevertheless proves schedule-independent undercoverage. It then reformulates the uniform sufficiency question on a to-be-specified response-regular subclass before asking whether \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\), \((n\kappa_n)^{-1/2}=o(t_n)\), and \(t_n=o(\kappa_n)\) suffice.

sampling_model.design: For fixed-law supporting results, regular samples jointly identify \(p\), \(r\), and \(\mu\). For uniform questions, row \(n\) contains independent observations from \(P_n^\circ\), with fixed finite supports and cell-probability floors indexed by \(\kappa_n\). The response-boundary counterexample uses uniform \(2\times2\) response-study cells, fixed deployment margins, and Bernoulli means \(\lambda/n\), so its obstruction is collapsing response variance rather than rare deployment or study cells.
sampling_model.units: Target contexts and actions are multinomial draws; separate interventional response units identify every finite \((c,x)\) cell. Dependence across stacked regular components is allowed through a declared row influence vector. In the singleton counterexample the margins are observed without error and only the four response means are sampled.
sampling_model.treatment: The response study observes micro action \(X\); target macro action \(h\) uses an unknown context-only selector calibrated to \(r\). The response-boundary theorem changes only the sampling law for the identified micro-response means and does not alter the causal selector class or target interval.
sampling_model.overlap: The class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) imposes floors on \(p_n\), \(r_n\), and \(\pi_n\), but no lower bound on Bernoulli response means, endpoint-relevant variances, or Gaussian anti-concentration. Consequently it contains the singleton response-boundary array even for a floor sequence satisfying \(n\kappa_n^3\to\infty\). The repaired uniform question must add a faithful response regularity condition before imposing any margin or tuning rates.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The stacked estimator and multiplier obey the assumed absolute bounded-Lipschitz approximations. The singleton theorem shows that these approximations can both converge to a degenerate Gaussian law while the all-zero sample event retains positive limiting probability, the multiplier critical value is zero, and the ridged endpoint estimate misses the true singleton interval. Uniform inference therefore needs response-side relative variance or anti-concentration control beyond the two existing approximation assumptions.

prose_updates.related_work: VanderWeele and Hernán show that multiple-version effects depend on a specified version-assignment distribution. Béal and Latouche apply that setup to PDX precision-medicine comparisons. D'Haultfoeuille, Gaillac, and Maurel, Section 2.1.1, Theorem 1 and Equation (4), characterize a sharp coefficient set under unlinked margins through transport; that result informs the discrete selector envelope. Rubenstein et al. and Beckers and Halpern inform the intervention and abstraction semantics. Xia and Bareinboim, Proposition 1 and Definition 6, supply the partial-projection condition instantiated by the semantic lemma; their Equation 11 canonical residual law is fixed and cannot span a positive-dimensional free-selector polytope. Felekis et al. inform the transport representation. Bonnans and Shapiro and Danskin directly supply the parametric linear-program sensitivity tools, while Hundrieser et al. study estimated-cost transport. Fang and Santos provide the general directional-inference framework, and Hong and Li supply the fixed-law numerical-delta corollary. Cho and Russell, Methodology, Theorem 3.2, obtain uniform inference for linear functionals defined by linear moment inequalities by bootstrapping randomly perturbed LP values. Their perturbation support is fixed and nonvanishing, and their procedure differs from the present row-feasible numerical delta. Gafarov, Main Results, Theorem 3, constructs uniformly valid confidence sets for sharp affine identified-set projections, including flat primal faces, by regularized support functions under uniform positive rank and slack constants. Voronin provides delta-conditioned uniform consistency and pointwise inference for an LP-value procedure. None of these comparator results turns absolute bounded-Lipschitz approximation into coverage at a collapsing response-variance boundary. The new singleton theorem isolates that missing prerequisite; the rare-margin rate boundary remains open only after an appropriate response-regular class is specified.
prose_updates.interpretation: For deployment analyses, fixed-support pointwise inference remains available at an interior law, including nonunique transport faces. A triangular-array claim that permits identified Bernoulli response means to approach zero requires more: good absolute Gaussian and multiplier approximation can coexist with a positive-probability all-zero study and severe undercoverage. Practitioners should therefore diagnose response-side effective information and variance calibration before applying a rare-margin numerical-step rule.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves a schedule-independent failure theorem for the specific paired numerical-delta confidence envelope on one collapsing-response singleton class. It does not prove a minimax impossibility for other confidence procedures and does not establish a sharp threshold in \(n\kappa_n^3\). The sufficient-regime and procedural-sharpness questions remain open on a repaired class whose additional response-interiority, nondegenerate-variance, relative variance-consistency, or anti-concentration condition must still be formulated without assuming coverage. The experiment class \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) itself has only margin and response-study cell floors. Cho--Russell and Gafarov already provide uniform LP inference using different constructions and regularity classes. The projected SCM construction, sharp selector image, endpoint certificates, fixed-map obstruction, cycle criterion, fixed-interior derivative, and pointwise numerical-delta result retain their supporting scope.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem is the required negative certificate showing that the two absolute bounded-Lipschitz approximation assumptions do not by themselves control simultaneous endpoint coverage at a collapsing response boundary.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem separates response-boundary degeneracy from rare-margin face switching: its fixed-margin singleton satisfies the approximation requirements and can be embedded in the proposed sufficient rate regime, yet every deterministic numerical schedule undercovers.
statement_notes.consumer: It tells users of the selector envelope that response-side variance and anti-concentration diagnostics are prerequisites for any uniform rare-cell tuning guarantee.

statement_notes.justification: The open sufficiency question is retained only on a response-regular subclass that excludes the proved singleton counterexample by primitive, independently checkable conditions.
statement_notes.gap: A minimal noncircular response-interiority, nondegenerate-variance, relative variance-consistency, or anti-concentration condition has not yet been fixed, and uniform face localization and quantile validity under the proposed margin-rate window remain unproved after that repair.
statement_notes.consumer: A positive answer would provide a usable simultaneous selector-envelope tuning regime together with explicit response-support or variance diagnostics required for its application.

added_lemmas.statement:
\textbf{Response-boundary failure under bounded-Lipschitz approximation.}
Under \(\mathrm{def:response\text{-}boundary\text{-}singleton}\), \(\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\).  The primitive and conditional multiplier bounded-Lipschitz approximations hold uniformly over this singleton class:
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}}
\sup_{\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{BL}}\leq1}
\left|
E_{\mathbb P}f\!\left(\sqrt n(\widehat\beta_n-\beta_n)\right)
-E f(G_{\mathbb P,n})
\right|\longrightarrow0,
\]
and, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}}
\Pr_{\mathbb P}\!\left(
\sup_{\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{BL}}\leq1}
\left|
E_{\mathbb P}^{\star}f(G_n^\star)-E f(G_{\mathbb P,n})
\right|>\epsilon
\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Nevertheless, the same \(\mathbb P^0\), selected independently of the numerical-delta schedule, satisfies
\[
\exists\,\mathbb P^0\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\quad
\forall\,t=(t_n)_{n\geq1}\ \text{with }t_n>0,qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left(
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right)
\leq 1-\exp(-\lambda)<1-\alpha.
\]
Thus bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximation, even uniformly over a singleton experiment class, does not by itself imply critical-value or coverage validity when response variance collapses.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For every row of \(\mathbb P^0\), the construction gives
\[
\min_{c\in\mathcal C}p_{n,c}=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}r_{n,x}=\frac12,
\qquad
\min_{(c,x)\in\mathcal C\times\mathcal X}\pi_{n,cx}=\frac14.
\]
Because \(0<\kappa_n\leq1/4\), both margin floors in \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}experiment}\) hold.  The observations are independent and the supports are fixed by construction.  Hence
\[
\mathbb P^0\in\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0},
\qquad
\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}=\lbrace\mathbb P^0\rbrace
\subseteq\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}.
\tag{1}
\]

Let
\[
D_n(\mathbb P)=
\sup_{\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{BL}}\leq1}
\left|
E_{\mathbb P}f\!\left(\sqrt n(\widehat\beta_n-\beta_n)\right)
-E f(G_{\mathbb P,n})
\right|
\]
and
\[
D_n^\star(\mathbb P)=
\sup_{\lVert f\rVert_{\mathrm{BL}}\leq1}
\left|
E_{\mathbb P}^{\star}f(G_n^\star)-E f(G_{\mathbb P,n})
\right|.
\]
The conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:vanishing\text{-}variance\text{-}all\text{-}zero\text{-}certificate}\), applied to the row laws in \(\mathrm{def:response\text{-}boundary\text{-}singleton}\), gives
\[
D_n(\mathbb P^0)\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{and}\quad
D_n^\star(\mathbb P^0)\longrightarrow_{\mathbb P^0}0.
\tag{2}
\]
Since \(\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}\) has exactly one element, (2) implies
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}}D_n(\mathbb P)
=D_n(\mathbb P^0)\longrightarrow0,
\tag{3}
\]
and, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}}
\Pr_{\mathbb P}\!\left(D_n^\star(\mathbb P)>\epsilon\right)
=
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left(D_n^\star(\mathbb P^0)>\epsilon\right)
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (3) and (4) are precisely the two asserted singleton-uniform bounded-Lipschitz approximations.

It remains to calculate coverage.  Define the all-zero event
\[
A_n=\bigcap_{i=1}^{n}\lbrace Y_{n,i}=0\rbrace.
\]
Every response has success probability \(\lambda/n\), independently of its cell label, so
\[
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}(A_n)
=\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^n
\longrightarrow\exp(-\lambda).
\tag{5}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:vanishing\text{-}variance\text{-}all\text{-}zero\text{-}certificate}\), on \(A_n\) all true costs equal \(\lambda/n\), all estimated costs equal \(a/n\), and the multiplier critical value is zero for every positive value of \(t_n\).  Because every coupling in \(\Gamma(p_n,r_n)\) has total mass one, these statements give
\[
L(\beta_n)=U(\beta_n)=\frac{\lambda}{n},
\qquad
F(\widehat\beta_n)=\left(\frac{a}{n},\frac{a}{n}\right),
\qquad
q_{1-\alpha,n}^\star=0
\quad\text{on }A_n.
\tag{6}
\]
Therefore, for every deterministic schedule with \(t_n>0\),
\[
\mathrm{CI}_n(t)=\left[\frac{a}{n},\frac{a}{n}\right]
\quad\text{on }A_n.
\tag{7}
\]
Since \(a<\lambda\), (6) and (7) show that, with
\[
E_n(t)=\left\lbrace[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]
\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\right\rbrace,
\]
one has \(A_n\subseteq E_n(t)^c\).  Consequently, by (5),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}(E_n(t))
\leq
\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(1-\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}(A_n)\right)
=1-\exp(-\lambda).
\tag{8}
\]
The experiment \(\mathbb P^0\) did not depend on \(t\), so (8) holds simultaneously for every deterministic positive schedule.  Finally, \(\lambda<-\log\alpha\) implies \(\exp(-\lambda)>\alpha\), and hence
\[
1-\exp(-\lambda)<1-\alpha.
\tag{9}
\]
Combining (1), (3), (4), (8), and (9) proves the theorem.  No rare-margin rate is used: the obstruction is the collapse of response variance and the resulting failure of quantile regularity.

The added theorem then gives schedule-independent undercoverage, even though both bounded-Lipschitz approximations are valid, so an affirmative answer to the old question would not identify rare-margin face switching or a sharp \(n\kappa_n^3\) threshold.  The proposed question honestly narrows the intended inquiry to a subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) satisfying a yet-to-be-characterized primitive nondegeneracy condition; it does not assume coverage.

proposed.name: response-boundary singleton experiment class
proposed.construction:
Fix \(\mathcal C=\mathcal X=\lbrace 1,2\rbrace\), a boundary sequence satisfying \(0<\kappa_n\leq 1/4\), and constants
\[
0<a<\lambda<\min\lbrace 1/2,-\log\alpha\rbrace.
\]
For row \(n\), let the deployment margins be known without error and equal to \(p_n=r_n=(1/2,1/2)\).  Let \(W_{n,1},\ldots,W_{n,n}\) be independent response-study cell labels, each uniform on \(\mathcal C\times\mathcal X\), and, conditionally on the labels, let the responses be independent with
\[
Y_{n,i}\mid W_{n,i}=(c,x)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\lambda/n).
\]
Thus \(\pi_{n,cx}=1/4\) and \(\mu_{n,cx}=\lambda/n\) for all \((c,x)\).  If \(\overline Y_{n,cx}\) is the within-cell response proportion, set to zero when the cell is empty, define
\[
\widehat\mu_{n,cx}=\left(1-\frac{2a}{n}\right)\overline Y_{n,cx}+\frac{a}{n},
\qquad
\widehat\beta_n=(p_n,r_n,\widehat\mu_n),
\]
and let \(G_n^\star\) be the empirical-influence multiplier draw for these response estimators with zero margin coordinates.  Denote the resulting row law by \(P_n^{\circ,0}\), the triangular-array experiment by \(\mathbb P^0=(P_n^{\circ,0})_{n\geq1}\), and the singleton experiment class by
\[
\mathfrak Q_{\kappa}=\lbrace\mathbb P^0\rbrace.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: This construction names the all-zero-event array, its ridge estimator and multiplier, and the mandated singleton class without asserting any of their load-bearing properties.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Characterize a minimal primitive uniform response-nondegeneracy or anti-concentration condition that excludes the response-boundary array without assuming coverage, and then determine whether bounded \(n\kappa_n^3\) forces schedule-quantified undercoverage through rare-margin optimal-face switching on that repaired subclass.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximations control absolute weak distance but impose no response-interiority, variance lower bound, relative variance consistency, or quantile anti-concentration.  They therefore allow a degenerate Gaussian limit and an atom at the limiting critical value, for which vanishing-width intervals miss an \(n^{-1}\)-scale ridge discrepancy with nonvanishing probability.
open_obligations.attempted: The two-context all-zero-event construction was evaluated for every positive numerical-delta schedule.  It proves genuine critical-value and coverage distortion, but that distortion persists independently of rare margins and so cannot certify procedural sharpness of the \(n\kappa_n^3\) boundary.  Reusing it as a rare-margin witness would misattribute the mechanism.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The all-zero response construction gives one fixed experiment \(\mathbb P^0\), independent of \(t\), for which both singleton-uniform bounded-Lipschitz approximation statements hold but
\[
\forall t=(t_n)_{n\geq1}\ \text{with }t_n>0,qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\Pr_{\mathbb P^0}\!\left(
[L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)
\right)
\leq1-\exp(-\lambda)<1-\alpha.
\]
This proves response-boundary failure but does not determine the rare-margin \(n\kappa_n^3\) threshold after response nondegeneracy is imposed.
